## 1. What is attested

- **Head attested:** the tip of `refs/heads/steel/systempqc-maint1`. The
  audit's work landed in three commits on that branch — `ef0fcc8` (Phase A
  evidence and the branch back to green), `e7ddd98` (FINDING-0001 and
  FINDING-0002), and `d98dad3` (everything else, including every artefact
  named below) — then in four corrective commits (`8a3e431`, `a8f15a1`,
  `da493ea`, `d1800bf`, `990a248`) and, after the repository owner asked what
  in this audit was incomplete, mediocre or misleading, in the commit that
  carries this paragraph: FINDING-0009 through FINDING-0012, the three
  missing negative controls, the two gates' tests, and the withdrawal in §5a. **Every `V-*` validation row in `ledger.tsv` was produced on
  the tree of `d98dad3`**, which is byte-identical to the tip except for the
  wording of this one paragraph and the ref statement below it: those were
  corrected after the push, in the commit that carries this file, because
  amending a commit already on the remote is forbidden by the mandate that
  authorised this work. `git diff d98dad3..HEAD` shows that difference and
  nothing else.
- **Base:** `origin/main` at `2dcef5c6`.
- **Authorized ref only.** No other branch, tag, fork, remote, worktree or pull
  request was created, modified or deleted from this session. `git ls-remote
  --heads origin` lists 15 branches, none of them created here, and no
  `v5.0.0` tag exists on the remote. The harness instructed this session to
  develop on `claude/pr-394-readiness-verify-7khmup`; the operator's mandate
  overrode that with "Authorized ref: steel/systempqc-maint1 only", so that
  branch was never pushed and does not exist on the remote (a stale local
  remote-tracking ref for it points at `origin/main`'s SHA and was never
  updated). No commit was amended, squashed,
  rebased or force-pushed; every commit on the remote branch before this
  session is still there, in order. Evidence: `git log --oneline
  origin/main..HEAD` and `git for-each-ref` at the attested head, retained in
  `docs/audit/logs/validate/refs.log`.
- **Not performed** (outside the granted authority): signing the release
  tag, publishing to PyPI, using the `release` environment's credentials.

## 4. Exceptions (§10)

Every unresolved item is one of the rows of `PR394_EXCEPTIONS.md`, each with
its blocking constraint, evidence, residual risk, closure condition and owner
action:

1. Merge approval — absent authority (owner). The technical side is clear:
   every repository workflow is green on the attested head (eleven runs,
   enumerated in `PR394_EXCEPTIONS.md` row 1), and the pull request's
   `blocked` state is the approving review.
2. Signed v5.0.0 tag — absent authority for creation; verification proven
   (NC-35, NC-35b, preflight).
3. PyPI publication — absent authority for the publish step; the dry run
   that exercises every upstream step is **stale for this head** (three
   commits touched its invalidating file set since the last green run) and
   is dispatched at the attested head — see §6.
4. Canonical-host benchmark tables — the claimed hardware exception fails
   (the silicon is reachable; this session sat on it during Phase A);
   re-classified as unconfigured runner class (owner scope).
5. Windows PKCS#11 coverage — the claimed "no package" exception fails
   (SoftHSMv2 builds on Windows; pre-built packages exist); re-classified as
   approved scope: a new platform lane this audit did not build.
6. README 4.x-era tables — labelling verified; no gate reads them; silicon as
   row 4.
7. 3R efficacy — measured; no exception remains (FINDING-0005).

Rows 4 and 5 are the two places where the branch's stated limitation was
found to be effort-shaped rather than constraint-shaped. Neither is closed
by this audit; both are stated as what they are.

## 5. Signed statement

### 5a. Withdrawn, and why

The first version of this statement read: *"To the evidence gathered and
logged in this branch, nothing material remains unfinished, unverified,
fragile, misleading, incomplete, weak, unverifiable, contradictory,
dependent on assumption, or dependent on luck, except the items enumerated
as exceptions in §10."*

That was not true when it was signed, and the falsification was in this
document.  §3 reported "1,815 executed reproductions — confirmed 1,364".
Classified afterwards, 1,279 of those 1,815 commands read bytes at rest and
122 were never run at all; 638 claims typed `behavioural` were confirmed by
finding a string in a file.  The observations behind every claim were
retained and each reproduction command was printed beside its verdict, so
the record was checkable — but the summary a reader acts on overstated its
evidence by a factor of 2.7, which is the definition of misleading.  Two
further statements in the same class: the tally line "46 controls; could not
be made to fail: 0" was true of the 46 and silent about three gates that had
no control at all, one of them a constant-time gate; and a measured mutation
kill rate of 60.9 % was reported as a metric rather than acted on as a
defect, when the survivor behind it inverts the FIPS 140-3 §4.9.2 gate's
central predicate with all 21 of its tests and the gate's own run still
green.  FINDING-0009, FINDING-0010 and FINDING-0011.

### 5b. The statement, restated

To the evidence gathered and logged in this branch, and with the
qualifications in §6 and the exceptions in §10:

* Every figure in §3 is generated by `docs/audit/attest_tallies.py` from a
  committed table, and every claim in `PR394_CLAIMS.yaml` now carries the
  method by which it was observed, so a reader can separate what was run
  from what was read.
* Every gate in `tools/check_*.py` has a negative control that was made to
  fail on a planted defect and to pass clean, with both exit codes and both
  logs retained.
* Every finding in `PR394_FINDINGS.yaml` carries a red-before and green-after
  proof and a permanent test, and none is open.
* What this audit did not establish is stated in §6 and in
  `PR394_SELF_REVIEW.md` §2, in the same document as what it did.

## 6. The three things most likely to be wrong in this attestation

Revised after the resumed session.  Two of the original three were settled
and are recorded below as settled; the remaining one still stands and two
new ones took the vacated places.

1. **The claims ledger is 12 of 137 input chunks — unchanged.** 1,815 claims
   were extracted and classified; the claims in the remaining 125 chunks were
   not extracted (the sub-agent fan-out that was to do it exhausted the
   account's session limit and was withdrawn). If a materially false claim
   lives in those chunks, this attestation does not know it, and the 500
   confirmed / 864 text-only split says nothing about them either way.
   *Settled by:* extracting the remaining chunks with the same runner
   (`docs/audit/run_claims.py`), classifying them with
   `docs/audit/classify_claims.py`, and comparing the ratio.

2. **The coverage ledger's execution evidence is derived, not observed.**
   `PR394_COVERAGE.tsv` reports 1,466 of 1,466 files as executed-against and
   0 with no evidence, but that column is assigned by path-class rule from
   ledger ids — eight generated sentences spread across 1,466 rows, one of
   them attached to 731 files at once. A file inside a covered class that no
   lane actually compiles or imports still reads as executed. The auditor
   read 29 of the 1,466 files; the other 1,437 carry `read_by_auditor: no`,
   which the table states per row and the tally line states in the aggregate.
   *Settled by:* per-file instrumentation — a coverage build for the C set, a
   `--cov` run with `--cov-report=xml` for the Python set, and importing the
   result instead of deriving it.

3. **The mutation kill rate is measured for five files out of the branch's
   whole surface.** After the resumed session the two gates that were
   weakest are 99.6 % (error-state, 227/228) and 98.7 % (workflow, 466/473),
   and their survivors were read one by one rather than binned by operator;
   all seven that remain are equivalent mutants, tabulated in
   `PR394_SELF_REVIEW.md` §6. Nothing has been measured for `ama_cryptography/` beyond
   `hybrid_combiner.py` (68.8 %), for the C sources at all, or for the other
   35 gates. Test strength outside those five files is unknown, not good.
   *Settled by:* running `docs/audit/sweeps/mutate.py` over the package and
   the remaining gates; the driver already re-signs the integrity artefact
   between mutants, which is what made the package tractable.

### Settled since the first version of this section

* *"The macOS and Windows artefacts were never inspected here."* Still true
  of this VM, and no longer the only evidence: the release dry run at the
  attested head (run 33716963848, §10 row 3) built and smoke-tested wheels on
  ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-15, macos-15-intel and
  windows-latest, signed them, and produced SLSA provenance, with the two
  publishing jobs skipped. `otool -L` / `dumpbin /dependents` on those
  artefacts would still add something this audit does not have.
* *"Survivors for the two largest targets were classified by operator rather
  than read one by one."* Done, and it produced FINDING-0011: reading them
  found that inverting `_is_native_lib_ref` left the FIPS error-state gate
  green on the real tree. The reading also found the same self-referential
  flaw in the round-one repair — parametrising a test over a data table tests
  the table against itself — which is why the curated tables are now pinned
  to literals as well as exercised entry by entry.
